She read it and immediately received a spiritual witness that it was true; Joseph had seen God the Father and His Son, Jesus Christ. She was taught and baptized and became an example to her parents, who joined the Church 19 years later.

We visited members whose neighborhoods were completely destroyed. “Our family is safe,” Cody and Haylee Woodbury said to me, “and our faith is secure. We can build another house.” Their faith in Jesus Christ lifted their courage, and their courage has elevated their faith.

He was crucified on the cross and, in the majesty of our Heavenly Father’s plan, rose the third day. Because He rose from the tomb, we too will be resurrected. How sublime are the purposes of our God and how immense is our reverence for our Savior.

talks.title: Integrity and Virtue Lead to Happiness

references.label: David O. McKay
references.excerpt: On the grounds of one building there is a replica of a message that significantly influenced President David O. McKay when he was a young missionary in Scotland.

references.label: Joseph Smith
references.excerpt: Among the touching guidance that Joseph Smith received in Liberty Jail is the declaration, “Let virtue garnish thy thoughts unceasingly.”

references.label: 2 Nephi 2:25
references.excerpt: Significantly President McKay taught: “Happiness is the purpose and design of existence. ‘Men are that they might have joy’ [see 2 Nephi 2:25]. Virtue, uprightness, faithfulness, holiness, and keeping the commandments of God lead to a happy life.”

references.label: Russell M. Nelson
references.excerpt: Lifelong disciples of Jesus Christ best reflect the Savior’s teaching and direction when they joyfully live lives of integrity and virtue. The covenant path that will return us to our beloved Father in Heaven and His Son, Jesus Christ, is not obscure; it is well marked. We have been repeatedly taught the principles and covenants essential for this sacred path.

references.label: Matthew 7:13–14
references.excerpt: The virtuous, Christlike life necessary to sustain us and propel us along the covenant path has never been more important or challenging. If we are to be spiritually prepared to have the integrity and virtue required of disciples of Jesus Christ, we can stay on the path and continue to follow wise, righteous principles that lead to happiness.

references.label: Russell M. Nelson
references.excerpt: As a new missionary, Elder McKay passed a building where the stone above the doorway bore this carved inscription: “WHAT-E’ER THOU ART ACT WELL THY PART.”

references.label: David O. McKay
references.excerpt: This message, “Whate’er thou art, act well thy part,” was so important and had such an impact on Elder McKay that he used it for inspiration as a missionary and for the rest of his life. He determined that whatever responsibility he had, he would do his very best.

references.label: David O. McKay
references.excerpt: In our day, the application of this principle is essential if we are to be true lifelong disciples of Christ. We need to live our lives with integrity and follow His example. The Lord, speaking of one servant in Nauvoo, declared, “He may be trusted because of the integrity of his heart.” Preach My Gospel teaches, “Integrity includes being honest with God, yourself, your leaders, and others.”

references.label: Matthew 5:3–11

True happiness, often translated as blessedness, is the actual outcome of integrity and being virtuous. Virtue includes not only a strong personal moral compass but also cleanliness, modesty, goodness, holiness, and reverence for the sacred.
